when: you have a kill or assist on their jungler before 4:00 and he is dead or just respawned
asks: i killed their jungler what now
got first blood on the jungler, do i invade
their jungler just died early, take his camps?
killed him in his jungle now what
say: Take the camps he left up on the side you killed him, then go home, or finish your own clear first if your health is low.
more: His camps are worth double: you gain them and he walks back to nothing, which widens the level gap for the first crab and the first gank.
Leave once the nearest enemy laner starts walking over. The second fight in their jungle goes to whoever gets help first.
If you are low, your own untouched camps are the same gold with no risk, and you still come out a level up.
check: Your own health, which of his camps are actually still up, and whether the enemy laner next to that side is pushed in or already missing.
breaks: Wrong if their nearest laner has the wave shoved and yours cannot follow: take one camp at most and leave, or just clear your own side.
basis: pro:An invade ends when the nearest lane arrives

when: you are a level or more above their jungler
asks: i'm a level up on their jungler how do i use it
i out level him what do i do
im ahead of their jungler now what
how do i punish their jungler being behind
say: Stand on the camps he has left and make him fight for them, or spend the level on a gank if your camps are down.
more: A jungler who is behind has very few places to farm. If you are waiting at the one camp he can reach, he either gives it or fights a level down.
Every camp he loses keeps the gap open for the next objective, where the level matters more than it does right now.
Ganking is the other use of the lead: a level up means your damage and health in a two on two are better than his if he shows.
check: Which of his camps are up, and whether the lanes beside that side of his jungle are pushed toward his tower or yours.
breaks: Wrong if the lanes next to his jungle are losing: their laners arrive first and the level lead does not cover a two on one. Farm your side and gank instead.
basis: pro:A jungler who is behind has few places to go

when: their jungler is dead with a respawn timer running
asks: their jungler is dead what do i take
enemy jungler just died, objective or camps
jungler's dead, do we do dragon
he's dead, what's free right now
say: Start whichever objective is up now, nobody can Smite against you, or take his camps on that side if none is up.
more: With their jungler dead there is no Smite against you, so the main question is whether their laners can stop you before it dies.
If nothing is up, his camps are the payment. He respawns behind on gold and with less to farm, which makes the next objective easier too.
Watch his respawn timer. Be walking out before it ends, not starting something new.
check: Whether a dragon, grubs or herald is actually alive right now, and how many enemy laners can walk to it.
breaks: Wrong if you are low or their laners are already moving to the pit with numbers: take the camps on the far side from them instead.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: you just got a kill or assist on their bot laner or support
asks: we killed bot what now
got a kill bot, dragon or tower
gank worked bot, what do i take
bot lane is dead do we dragon
say: Take dragon with your bot lane if it's up, or help shove the wave into their tower for plates if it isn't.
more: A kill only pays when something on the map follows it. Dragon or tower plates are the two things beside bot lane that turn it into a lasting lead.
Shoving the wave first matters either way: the dead laners lose minions under tower, and your bot lane gets a free recall afterward.
After that, go back to your camps. They kept respawning while you were in lane.
check: Whether dragon is alive, where their jungler is, and whether your bot lane has the health to stay.
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is alive nearby and your bot lane is low: shove the wave and leave, do not start dragon.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

when: you just got a kill or assist on their top laner, game time is after 8:00
asks: we killed top what now
top gank worked, grubs?
got their top laner, what do i do
top is dead, herald or plates
say: Take grubs or herald, whichever's up, with your top laner while theirs is dead, or hit plates with the wave if the pit's empty.
more: Their top laner is the one who would normally arrive first to contest the top pit, so his death timer is your window.
If the pit is empty, a crashed wave plus plates makes your top laner strong enough to hold the side alone later, which frees you for the other half of the map.
Do not stay for a second kill. Your camps on the other side are waiting.
check: What is in the top pit right now, where their jungler and mid are, and whether your top laner has the health to help.
breaks: Wrong if their jungler and mid are both alive and their mid has the wave pushed: they collapse on the pit. Take plates and go.
basis: pro:Count what the map pays for a dive or collapse

when: you have a kill lead and enough gold for an item component or more
asks: i have a lot of gold should i back
do i recall or keep going
i'm fed but haven't backed
should i go spend my gold
say: Recall now and bring the item to the next fight, or clear one more camp first if it's right beside you and nothing is spawning.
more: Gold in your pocket is not strength. The lead only exists once it is bought, and the other jungler may already have spent his.
Time the recall so you arrive at the next objective with the item, instead of showing up with more gold and the same stats.
Skipping the recall keeps your camp pace, but you walk into the next skirmish weaker than your score says.
check: How long until the next objective, and whether your camps are up or down right now.
breaks: Wrong if an objective spawns within the walk back: stay and contest with what you have, then recall straight after.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: you have more kills than their jungler but lower CS
asks: i have kills but less farm, am i ahead
i'm fed but my cs is bad
i've been ganking a lot is that ok
i got kills but he out farms me
say: You're not really ahead yet. Clear your camps before the next gank, or gank only the lane you pass on the way.
more: Kills fade if the other jungler quietly took every camp while you were in lanes. His levels arrive later but they do arrive.
Full clears between ganks keep both: the gold from kills and the levels from camps. That combination is what wins the mid game objectives.
If your camps are down, then ganking is free and you should keep doing it.
check: Which of your camps are up right now, and how the two junglers' levels compare.
breaks: Wrong if your camps are all down or a lane is one kill away from winning for good: gank, then clear.
basis: pro:Kills are not a lead if the farm went the other way

when: one allied laner has two or more kills and is above their opponent in level
asks: my top is fed who do i play for
one lane is winning hard do i keep helping
should i camp the winning lane
my mid is fed what do i do with that
say: Clear toward the fed lane and set up its tower or the nearby objective, or cover the weakest lane once if its tower's about to fall.
more: A winning lane makes the jungle next to it safer for you. Their laner struggles to leave the wave, so objectives on that side get much cheaper.
End your clears on that side so you are already there when the wave crashes. Tower gold plus an objective is how one fed lane becomes a team lead.
The lane you leave alone gets nothing from you, so decide on purpose which one that is.
check: Whether the fed laner's wave is pushing, and how close the losing lane's tower is to falling.
breaks: Wrong if the fed laner is a champion who wins the lane alone anyway: your time is worth more keeping a second lane alive.
basis: pro:End the clear beside the lane that matters

when: your team is ahead in kills and towers
asks: we're ahead how do i not throw
we're winning what should i avoid
how do we close this without throwing
we have a lead what do i do now
say: Set up at the next objective early and let them walk into you, or take their jungle camps if they won't come.
more: The team that is ahead does not need to chase. The team that is behind has to come to the objective, and they come through dark jungle you already hold.
Most leads are thrown by one player caught alone before a spawn. Arrive alive and on time and the lead does the work.
If they refuse to contest, their camps are the tax. A team with no jungle farm falls further behind without a fight.
check: Which objective is next and when, and whether your team is actually grouped with you.
breaks: Wrong if your teammates are spread across side lanes: do not stand in their jungle alone. Farm your own side until they group.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: an enemy outer tower has just fallen
asks: we took a tower what now
first tower's down where do i go
tower fell, do i invade
outer tower is gone what does that open
say: Move into their jungle on that side with a laner and take camps, or bring the same group to the next tower.
more: An outer tower was their vision and their safe ground. With it gone, the camps behind it are no longer safely theirs.
Taking those camps starves their jungler and puts you between them and the objective on that side.
Grouping for a second tower is the faster way to snowball, but it shows all of you on the map. Camps are slower and quieter.
check: Whether a laner is coming with you, and where their team was last seen.
breaks: Wrong if three or more of them are missing and nobody is with you: stay on your half until someone shows.
basis: pro:Outer towers are vision

when: your team is ahead and game time is past 20:00
asks: should we do baron
we're ahead is baron a good idea
do we start baron or wait
can we just take baron
say: Stand near Baron and catch whoever comes to check it, or start it properly if two of them are dead or showing far away.
more: With a lead, Baron works as bait first. They have to walk in to see it, and they walk in one at a time.
Starting it with all five of them alive turns your lead into a coin flip on Smite while you are low.
Win the fight at the pit, then take Baron with nobody left to contest.
check: How many of them are alive and where they last showed, and whether your side waves are pushed out.
breaks: Wrong if your side lanes are pushing into you: someone has to leave to catch them and the setup falls apart. Fix the waves first.
basis: pro:With a lead, Baron is bait before it is a prize

when: your team is ahead and an objective spawns soon
asks: how do i set up for the objective when ahead
we're ahead, what do i do before dragon
what should happen before we go baron
how do we prep the next objective
say: Have the side waves pushed before you walk to the pit, or take their camps beside it if the waves are already out.
more: A wave pushing into their tower pulls one of them away from the pit, and that is how a five on five becomes a five on four.
As the jungler you are the one who can ask for it and wait. Their camps by the pit pay you for the waiting.
Showing up early with bad waves just means standing there while your towers take damage.
check: Where the side waves are, since the coach cannot see them, and how long until the spawn.
breaks: Wrong if the objective is already up and they are starting it: go now with whoever is close and contest, waves or not.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: your team just won a fight with two or more enemies dead
asks: we won the fight what do we take
they're dead what now
ace, what do we do
fight's won, objective or tower
say: Take the biggest thing their dead players can't defend, a tower or the objective that's up, or reset together if you're all low.
more: A won fight pays nothing by itself. It pays in whatever you take during their death timers.
Check the longest respawn timer. That is how long you have, and it decides whether a tower, an objective or both fit.
Chasing the survivors past a tower is how a won fight turns into an even one.
check: Your team's health, which objective is alive, and where the waves are.
breaks: Wrong if everyone is low and their survivors are healthy: push the waves, recall, and walk back out with items.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

when: your team has two dragons and the enemy has none or one
asks: we have two dragons what now
we're ahead on drakes, what's the plan
how do we get soul
do we need the next dragon
say: Be at the next dragon early with vision, it puts you one from soul, or take the top pit objective if they stack five at dragon.
more: The dragon that puts you on soul point is the one a trailing team has to fight. Expect all of them, and arrive first so they walk into you.
If they send everyone, something on the other side of the map is free. Taking it keeps the lead growing while the dragon timer stays theirs to worry about.
Four dragons give the soul, so every one you bank now shortens the game.
check: The dragon respawn timer, and how many of them show on the bottom side.
breaks: Wrong if they are much stronger in a grouped fight right now: trade for the top side and fight the following dragon with another item.
basis: pro:A second objective moves the fight

when: you are ahead and the enemy team has scaling champions
asks: we're ahead but they scale what do i do
they out scale us how do i end faster
how do i speed the game up
they have late game champs and we're winning early
say: Take every dragon as it spawns to put a clock on them, or dive the weakest lane with numbers if no objective is up.
more: Against a scaling team your lead has an expiry date. Early dragons are the clock: soul can arrive before their items do.
They would rather farm than fight, so most early objectives are yours if you simply show up for each one.
Do not coast. An even game late favors that kind of team, so the lead has to turn into objectives now.
check: Dragon timers, and whether your lanes can move to the river before theirs.
breaks: Wrong if contesting means fighting five into their defensive setup while a lane is low: take the objective on the other side instead.
basis: pro:Early dragons are the clock against a scaling team

when: you have more kills than deaths and an objective spawns within about a minute
asks: i'm fed assassin what do i do
who do i kill before dragon
should i look for a pick
i'm ahead as an assassin how do i use it
say: Catch one of them walking to the objective and start it a player up, or stay with your team if nobody walks alone.
more: A pick is worth most just before a spawn. The death timer covers the objective, so one kill becomes a kill plus the dragon or Baron.
A pick long before the spawn is only gold. They respawn and arrive on time.
If they move as five, your job changes: wait behind your front line and go on the carry once the fight starts.
check: The objective timer and which of them tends to walk in alone.
breaks: Wrong if you have to cross their vision to find the pick: you become the one who is caught. Hold with your team.
basis: pro:Time the pick against the objective clock

when: your CS and level are above their jungler's
asks: i'm a farming jungler and i'm ahead, do i keep farming
i out farm him do i need to gank
i'm up in cs what now
should i just keep full clearing
say: Keep full clearing and add his camps on the side your lanes push, or gank once when all your camps are down.
more: Your lead is tempo. Each clear you finish first gives you a free window to take one of his camps before yours respawn.
Two jungles of farm reaches your item spikes minutes before he reaches his, and that is when you take over objectives.
Ganks are still fine when nothing is up to farm. That is the moment a gank costs you nothing.
check: Which lanes of yours are pushing, because that decides which side of his jungle is safe to enter.
breaks: Wrong if your team is losing every lane: farming alone will not hold the map. Cover a lane before its tower goes.
basis: pro:Gank when your camps are down

when: you are ahead in level and items on a tank jungler
asks: i'm a tank and i'm ahead how do i use it
fed tank jungle what do i do
i'm ahead on a tank, do i start fights
how does a tank carry a lead
say: Start the fight at the next objective while your engage is ready, or stand in front and make them come through you.
more: A tank's lead makes the first engage hard to punish. You survive long enough for your carries to do the work.
Engage on whoever steps up first to check the pit. One caught player before the objective usually decides it.
Do not use the lead to dive deep alone. It is only worth something with your team behind you.
check: Whether your damage dealers are close enough to follow, and whether your engage ability is up.
breaks: Wrong if your carries are behind or not there yet: hold the engage, peel for them, and let the enemy start it.
basis: pro:Arrive together or do not arrive

when: you have a kill lead and are level 6 or higher
asks: i'm fed on belveth what now
how do i snowball belveth
belveth ahead what do i take
should i fight or farm on belveth when ahead
say: Keep taking large monsters and takedowns for permanent attack speed, or start the objective when their jungler shows on the far side.
more: Death in Lavender gives permanent attack speed for large monsters and champion takedowns, so every camp and kill makes the next one faster.
Forty passive stacks give a ninety second True Form and eighty make it permanent, so every camp you take while ahead is progress toward that as well.
Royal Maelstrom gives lifesteal and damage reduction, which lets you fight inside their jungle, but it roots you while it runs.
check: Your passive stack count, where their jungler last showed, and whether their crowd control has been used.
breaks: Wrong if they have several stuns ready: you get locked down mid channel. Farm their camps instead of fighting into them.
basis: kit:Bel'Veth

when: you are level 6 or higher and ahead of their jungler in level
asks: i'm ahead on khazix what do i do
kha zix fed how do i snowball
where do i find kills as khazix
khazix ahead, invade or gank
say: Hunt their jungler alone in his own jungle, he's isolated there, or catch a side laner who walks back to lane alone.
more: Unseen Threat marks enemies who are away from their allies, and Taste Their Fear hits harder on them. A jungler at his own camp is the cleanest case.
Void Assault makes you invisible, which is how you get on top of him or get out if a laner arrives.
Each time he dies at a camp he loses the camp too, so the gap keeps growing without you needing lanes to cooperate.
check: Whether the target is truly alone, with no minions or allies beside him.
breaks: Wrong if their laners on that side have the wave pushed: they arrive and you are the one outnumbered. Catch someone on the way to lane instead.
basis: kit:Kha'Zix

when: you have more kills than deaths and at least one finished item
asks: i'm fed on master yi how do i not throw
yi ahead what do i do in fights
master yi fed, do i go in
how do i teamfight as fed yi
say: Let someone else start the fight and come in after their stuns are used, or keep farming both jungles until one starts.
more: Alpha Strike makes you untargetable and Highlander ignores slows, but neither saves you from a stun you walk into first.
Going in second means their control is already spent on your front line, and then nobody can stop you cleaning up.
A fed Yi who dies first hands over the bounty and the fight together, which is the usual way this lead is thrown.
check: Which of their crowd control abilities have already been used in the fight.
breaks: Wrong if your team has nobody who can start a fight: take picks on lone targets in the jungle rather than waiting forever.
basis: kit:Master Yi

when: you are level 6 and ahead, and an enemy side laner has died at least once
asks: i'm ahead on nocturne where do i ult
nocturne level 6 what now
who do i paranoia
nocturne fed how do i snowball
say: Use Paranoia on the side lane that's already losing and take its tower after, or hold it for the next objective fight.
more: Paranoia cuts their vision of each other and lets you launch onto a champion, so a laner who is already behind gets no warning and no help.
A kill plus the tower opens that side of their jungle for the rest of the game.
Holding it for an objective is the safer use: their team cannot see who you are diving until you land.
check: Whether your laner there is healthy enough to follow, and whether the target has an escape ready.
breaks: Wrong if your laner there is low or dead: you land alone under a tower. Farm until the ult lines up with a lane that can help.
basis: kit:Nocturne

when: you are level 6 or higher and ahead of their jungler
asks: evelynn ahead what do i do
i'm fed on eve where do i go
evelynn level 6 how do i snowball
who do i gank as evelynn
say: Gank whichever lane is pushed toward your tower, camouflage gives them little warning, or take their camps if every lane is pushed up.
more: After level 6 Demon Shade gives you camouflage, so wards matter much less and an overextended laner has almost no warning.
Allure needs a moment before the charm is ready, so mark the target early and wait for it.
Last Caress makes you untargetable for a moment, hits the area in front of you and throws you a long way backward, which makes greedy angles safer than they look.
check: Which enemy laners are pushed past the middle of the lane, and whether they have a control ward down, since that reveals you.
breaks: Wrong if lanes are all shoved into their towers: there is no angle. Farm, and wait for a wave to bounce back.
basis: kit:Evelynn

when: your team is ahead in kills and an allied laner is alive in that lane
asks: can we dive
should i dive this lane
he's low under tower do we go
is a tower dive worth it
say: Dive only with a big wave already hitting the tower, then take plates, or wait a wave if it isn't there yet.
more: A dive runs on minions. The wave takes the tower shots and denies him the farm when he dies.
It also depends on one button: whatever he has to stall with. If that is down, the dive is close to free.
Count what it pays. A kill, a lost wave for him and plates is a real lead. A kill for a death is nothing.
check: How low the enemy laner really is, the size of the wave at the tower, whether their defensive spell or ability was used, and where their jungler is.
breaks: Wrong if their jungler has not shown and could be behind the tower: you turn a lead into a two for one against you.
basis: pro:A dive runs on minions and one defensive button

when: their jungler or highest-kill player died in the last few seconds
asks: their carry is dead what can we do
their jungler just backed, is that a window
they're down one what now
enemy adc is dead do we force
say: Force the objective or tower right now while they're a player short, or take deep vision if nothing is ready to hit.
more: Their strongest player being off the map is the cheapest moment to start anything. They either give it or fight without him.
The window is his respawn timer plus the walk back, so start immediately rather than grouping slowly.
If nothing can be taken, wards in their jungle make the next window easier to find.
check: The respawn timer, or whether you actually saw him recall since the coach cannot see recalls, and what is within reach before he is back.
breaks: Wrong if your own team is split or low: the window closes before you arrive. Reset so you are ready for the next one.
basis: pro:Their jungler or carry in base is your window

when: your team is ahead and three or more enemies are dead
asks: they're dead do we end
can we end the game
end or baron
three dead what do we do
say: Go for their base if a wave's with you and the timers are long, or take Baron or Elder and end on the next push.
more: Late respawn timers are long enough that a wave and a few players can finish the game outright.
Without a wave, towers hit you and time runs out. Baron or Elder then makes the next push the one that ends it.
Pick one and commit. Splitting between the two is how late leads are lost.
check: Whether a minion wave is near their base, how long the respawn timers are, and how many of you are alive.
breaks: Wrong if their inhibitor towers are all standing and no wave is close: take the objective, not the base.
basis: pro:One call at an objective: finish it or fight

when: you have a large kill lead and have not died recently
asks: i have a bounty how do i play
i'm really fed what should i avoid
how do i keep my lead
what's the safe way to play fed
say: Move with at least one teammate into their jungle and keep taking camps, or stay on your half when nobody can come.
more: Once you are far ahead, your death is the best thing that can happen to them. It pays a bounty and frees the next objective.
With one teammate beside you the same invades are safe, and you still strip their jungle.
The lead grows from farm and objectives. It does not need a risky extra kill.
check: Whether a teammate is actually near you, and how many of them are missing from the map.
breaks: Wrong if their whole team is showing on the far side: then going in alone is fine. Take what is free and leave.
basis: written

when: game time is around 8:00 and your top laner is ahead of theirs in level or kills
asks: should i do grubs
are grubs worth it
grubs or dragon
do i go for void grubs
say: Take grubs with your top and mid if they've got their waves pushed, or trade them for dragon if their team shows top.
more: Grubs are one window and they do not come back, so a team that is ahead on top side should bank them.
Price them against what you give up. Three people at the top pit means bot lane is alone, and their jungler can take dragon or dive.
Either way take one of the two. Giving both is the outcome to avoid.
check: Whether your top and mid can move first, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: Wrong if your lanes are pushed in and theirs arrive first: you lose the fight and the grubs. Cross the map and take dragon.
basis: pro:Price grubs against plates and waves

when: your team has taken herald and a dragon spawns soon
asks: where do i use herald
should herald go mid
herald mid or side lane
what does mid tower give us
say: Use herald mid before the dragon so the river is yours, or put it in the side lane that's one push from falling.
more: Their mid outer tower is what lets their mid laner stand safely near both rivers. Without it your team usually gets to dragon first.
A side tower is more gold for one laner, but it opens less of the map.
Decide by the next objective: if a dragon is coming, mid is the lane that buys it.
check: The dragon timer and how much health each of their outer towers has.
breaks: Wrong if their mid tower is nearly full health and a side tower is almost dead: take the sure tower.
basis: pro:Herald in mid before a dragon buys the river

when: you died before 4:00
asks: i died in my first clear what do i do
i got invaded and died
died early in the jungle now what
i just died at level 2
say: Clear the camps farthest from where you died, he's likely still on that side, or cover a lane wave if they're all gone.
more: After an early death the obvious camp is the one he expects you at. The far side of your own jungle is the safe farm.
You are a level down now, so skip any even fight with him until a full clear brings you back. One clear gets you to about level 4.
If your camps were taken, a wave from a laner who has recalled is experience that would otherwise be lost.
check: Which of your camps are still up, and whether their jungler showed anywhere after the kill.
breaks: Wrong if he showed on the far side already: then the side where you died is the free one. Go back there.
basis: pro:A jungler who is behind has few places to go

when: their jungler is a level or more above you
asks: their jungler is ahead of me what do i do
i'm a level down on their jungler
he out levels me how do i play
enemy jungler is stronger than me
say: Farm on the opposite side from where he last showed and gank from there, or ping your lanes back if he hasn't shown.
more: Do not mirror a stronger jungler. If you meet him in the river a level down, you lose the fight and the camps behind it.
Playing the opposite side trades with him. He gets his play, you get yours, and you do not die.
Levels even out through full clears with no deaths. That is the only reliable way the gap closes.
check: Where he last showed, and which of your lanes are pushed in.
breaks: Wrong if he keeps showing on the side with your only winning lane: then you have to be there, with that laner beside you.
basis: pro:The jungle beside a losing lane is theirs

when: your CS is well below their jungler's before 5:00 and you have not died
asks: he took my buff what do i do
i got counter jungled
my camps are gone
he stole my camps now what
say: Clear what's left on your side now, then cross to his far camps if he was just seen in yours, or cover a lane if not.
more: Time he spent in your jungle is time his own far side sat untouched. That is where the trade is.
You only know that trade is safe if he showed. If he vanished, assume he went back to his own camps.
A lane wave is the fallback. It is experience with a tower beside it.
check: Whether he was seen in your jungle in the last few seconds, and which of your lanes can help you on his side.
breaks: Wrong if his lanes on that far side are pushed up: his laners collapse on you. Take the lane wave instead.
basis: pro:Time in their jungle is time given away

when: your level and CS are below their jungler's
asks: i'm behind in farm do i gank or farm
i'm way behind what do i do
how do i catch up in the jungle
i'm down cs should i just farm
say: Full clear both sides without stopping, twice if you can, or take a gank only if it's on your path and the laner's low.
more: Camps are the one income nobody has to hand you. Two uninterrupted clears do more for a deficit than a hopeful gank.
A failed gank when behind costs double: no kill, and your camps sit up while he farms his.
A gank on your path costs almost nothing, which is why that one exception is worth taking.
check: Which camps are up, and whether any enemy laner is low and pushed up on your route.
breaks: Wrong if a lane is about to lose its tower to dives: show there once to stop it, then go back to farming.
basis: pro:An early gank is paid for in camps

when: two or more allied laners are behind their opponents in CS and level
asks: all my lanes are losing what do i do
every lane is behind
my team is losing everywhere
who do i help when everyone is losing
say: Pick the one lane that can still carry and end every clear beside it, or just farm and scale if none of them can.
more: You cannot fix three lanes. Spreading out means each gets a little help and all three still lose.
One lane kept alive gives your team a side of the map where objectives can be contested later.
The lanes you leave should be told to give ground and farm under tower.
check: Which laner has the champion that scales or carries best, and whether their wave is in a place you can gank.
breaks: Wrong if the lane you chose keeps dying anyway: stop, and put your time into your own farm.
basis: pro:The lane without help gives nothing

when: an allied laner is dead or just recalled and you are behind
asks: my laner died should i take the wave
can i take lane farm
do i catch the wave
top is dead do i go cover
say: Catch the wave at the tower if you're close, it's gold and experience your team loses otherwise, or stay on camps if it's far.
more: A wave dying to the tower is lost for everyone. Taking it puts you back toward level pace and saves your laner from a worse return.
It also keeps plates on the tower, which matters more when you are behind.
Only take what would be lost. Leave the next wave for the laner.
check: How close the wave is to your tower, and whether the enemy laner is still there with their jungler.
breaks: Wrong if both their laner and jungler are at that tower: you get dived. Give the wave and keep your camps.
basis: written

when: their jungler has two or more kills and your CS is behind his
asks: he keeps invading me
their jungler is in my jungle all the time
i can't farm my own jungle
how do i stop getting invaded
say: Give the side beside your losing lane and farm the other, or clear it only while that laner has the wave pushed.
more: A fed jungler invades where his laners can follow. That side is his until the lane next to it stops losing.
Farming the other half keeps you alive and leveling, which is the only way the gap ever closes.
A ward at the entrance he uses turns the next invade from a death into a warning.
check: Which of your lanes has the wave pushed, and where he was last seen.
breaks: Wrong if he shows on the opposite side of the map: that is the moment to take your contested camps quickly.
basis: pro:The jungle beside a losing lane is theirs

when: an objective is up and your team is behind in kills
asks: we can't contest dragon what do i do
do i give the objective
we're behind should we fight for it
they're doing dragon what now
say: Give it and take something on the far side straight away, camps or a tower, or contest only if they start it short a player.
more: If you cannot win the fight, standing near the pit gains nothing and risks a pick. The trade has to start the moment they commit.
Their jungler is at the pit, so his far camps and the far side lane are unguarded for that time.
The trade needs something real. A few camps and tower plates count. Walking around does not.
check: How many of them are at the objective, and what is actually takeable on the other side.
breaks: Wrong if this objective is their soul or it ends the game for them: then you have to contest with whatever you have.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

when: the enemy has one or two dragons and your team has none
asks: they have two dragons are we losing
do we need to stop their dragons
they keep taking dragon
when do we have to fight for dragon
say: Trade the early ones for top side and fight the dragon that would put them on soul point, or sooner if you spike first.
more: Early dragons are small on their own. Dying for one while behind costs more than the dragon gives them.
The one before soul point is different. Four give soul, so the third is where you draw the line.
Use the time you gave up to get items, so that fight happens on your terms.
check: Their dragon count and the next dragon timer.
breaks: Wrong if their team scales harder than yours: giving dragons only helps them. Contest earlier, while you are still stronger.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: their jungler is above you in level and an objective is being contested
asks: i can't out smite him
how do i steal it when i'm behind
he always wins smite
what do i do at the pit when behind
say: Have your team go on their jungler first so Smite isn't a contest, or zone the pit entrance and don't walk in.
more: Smite fights are close to a coin flip, and the jungler who is ahead has more damage to finish with. Removing him from the pit is more reliable.
If you cannot reach him, holding the entrance at least keeps your team alive and may catch someone leaving low.
Walking into the pit alone to try for a steal is the trade they want.
check: Whether their jungler is standing where your team can reach him.
breaks: Wrong if he is safely behind their front line: do not force it. Take the trade on the other side of the map.
basis: pro:If you cannot win the Smite duel, remove their jungler

when: your level is below their jungler's and you are on a tank
asks: i'm behind on a tank am i useless
tank jungle behind what do i do
how do i help when i'm behind as tank
i'm behind but i have cc
say: Stay beside your strongest carry and use your crowd control on whoever dives them, or engage only when a pick is certain.
more: Crowd control does not fall behind the way damage does. A stun is just as long with no items.
What you lose is the health to start fights. Peeling keeps you useful without asking you to survive their whole team.
A fed carry who stays alive wins fights that your own gold never could.
check: Who on your team is actually doing damage, and who on theirs wants to dive them.
breaks: Wrong if your team has no carry who is ahead: then a pick on a lone target is the only way in, so look for that.
basis: written

when: you have more deaths than kills and are on an assassin
asks: i'm behind on an assassin what do i do
i can't kill anyone
assassin jungle behind how do i play
i do no damage now
say: Farm to your next item and go only for targets a level or more below you, or follow up after a teammate starts.
more: An assassin who is behind cannot kill a full-health target alone. Trying is how the gap doubles.
Check the scoreboard for levels. Whoever on their team is lowest is your target, usually a support or a laner who has died a lot.
Coming in second, after their abilities are used on someone else, works even from behind.
check: Whether the target is alone and whether they have their escape or protective spell.
breaks: Wrong if their whole team groups and nobody is alone: stop looking for kills and take camps and side waves until an item completes.
basis: written

when: you are behind in level and are on a farming champion
asks: i'm behind on a scaling jungler
farming jungler behind what now
i got set back, do i still just farm
how do i recover on a farm champ
say: Keep full clearing and take waves nobody is catching, or join only fights your team starts next to your camps.
more: Your champion wins by reaching items, and being behind only moves that time later. The plan still works if you stop dying.
Every fight you walk across the map for is a clear you did not do.
Tell your lanes you are farming so they play back. Silence is what gets them killed.
check: Camp timers, and whether a fight is close enough to reach without leaving camps up.
breaks: Wrong if the enemy is about to take soul or an inhibitor: farming through that loses the game. Go and defend.
basis: written

when: you are behind and level 6 or higher
asks: karthus behind what do i do
i'm behind on karthus
how do i catch up as karthus
karthus fell behind, farm or fight
say: Keep farming and press Requiem whenever a fight leaves them low, or stand in the fight if it's right beside your camp.
more: Requiem hits every enemy champion wherever you are, so you can collect assists and kills without leaving your camps.
That makes Karthus one of the few junglers who catches up while farming.
If you do die in a fight, Death Defied lets you keep casting for a while, so dying in the middle of them is not wasted.
check: The enemy health bars during fights elsewhere, since the coach sees deaths but not exact health.
breaks: Wrong if their team has healing or shields saving low targets: hold Requiem for the fight you are actually in.
basis: kit:Karthus

asks: my ganks keep failing
i keep ganking and getting nothing
should i gank that lane again
why are my ganks not working
say: Stop going there. Clear, then try the opposite side, or come back only once that enemy has used Flash.
more: A lane that has dodged two ganks is warded or holding its escape. A third try costs a third set of camps.
The other side of the map has had no jungler for minutes and is usually less careful.
Summoner spells are the thing that changes it. A target without Flash is a different gank.
check: Whether you really have ganked that lane twice for nothing, whether that enemy still has Flash, and where they place their wards.
breaks: Wrong if that lane is your only win condition: keep going, but come from a different angle or with a second teammate.
basis: pro:Stop repeating a gank that keeps failing

when: your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: which fights do we skip
we're behind do we fight
should i join that fight
how do we stop losing fights
say: Skip any fight in the river or their jungle and defend at your towers, or fight only when they're short a player.
more: When you are behind, an even fight on neutral ground is a loss. Towers and a short walk from base are what even the numbers.
Watch death timers and who shows in a side lane. Four against five near your tower is the fight you can win.
Each fight you decline also buys farm time, which is how the item gap narrows.
check: How many of them are visible and grouped, and whether your team is all there.
breaks: Wrong if giving ground means losing an inhibitor or soul: then you fight, as five and from your side.
basis: pro:Count who can actually arrive before contesting

when: your team is behind and Baron is alive
asks: we're behind late what do we do
how do we come back late game
they're going to take baron
is this game still winnable
say: Clear side waves and keep wards near Baron so you can catch one of them, or defend base if they group five.
more: Late game one pick is worth an objective, because respawn timers are long. A team that is ahead often gets careless around Baron.
Pushed side waves force someone to leave their group. That is the player to catch, or the number advantage to fight on.
You do not have to win the game back in one play. One good fight and Baron resets it.
check: Where their players are when they check Baron, and whether your waves are out.
breaks: Wrong if they are already hitting Baron with five and you have no vision: do not walk in blind. Hold your base.
basis: pro:A pushed side wave pulls a carry away from the pit

when: a fight has started and one or more allies are already dead
asks: my team is fighting do i go
should i join them
they're fighting without me
do i go help or not
say: If you can't reach it before it's decided, take a camp or wave nearby, or go in only if the enemy is the one outnumbered.
more: Arriving one at a time feeds a fight that is already lost. Each late arrival is another kill for them.
The scoreboard shows who is dead on both sides. Count the living before you start walking.
What you take elsewhere in those seconds is the only gain your team gets from that fight.
check: How far away the fight is and how healthy the survivors on both sides are.
breaks: Wrong if your arrival makes it even and their survivors are low: go, a late cleanup can flip it.
basis: pro:Arrive together or do not arrive

when: your level is below their jungler's and you are holding unspent gold
asks: i'm behind should i recall
do i back or keep farming when behind
is it worth backing for a small item
should i buy now
say: Recall and buy the component now, small stats matter most when you're behind, or finish the camp you're on first.
more: When you are behind, you cannot afford to walk into the next skirmish with gold unspent. The other jungler has probably spent his.
A recall also resets your health, which stops the easy invade on a low jungler.
Time it for when your camps are down so it costs the least.
check: Your gold against the component you want, and which camps are up.
breaks: Wrong if an objective you must defend spawns in seconds: stay, and recall right after.
basis: pro:Skipping the recall keeps camp pace but not power

when: you are behind in level
asks: zac behind what do i do
i'm behind on zac
how do i come back as zac
zac jungle fell behind
say: Gank from long range with Elastic Slingshot where they have no ward, or farm until Let's Bounce is ready for an objective fight.
more: Elastic Slingshot launches you in from far outside normal gank range, so the angle works even when you are low on stats.
Let's Bounce bounces four times, knocking up and slowing enemies it hits. That is the same value in a fight whether you are ahead or behind.
Cell Division lets you reform after fatal damage if the blobs survive, so being first in is less costly for you than for most.
check: Whether the lane has a ward covering the spot you would jump from.
breaks: Wrong if the laner you are jumping to help is too low to follow: you land alone. Pick another lane or keep farming.
basis: kit:Zac

when: you are behind in level and are level 6 or higher
asks: sejuani behind what do i do
i'm behind on sejuani
how do i help as sejuani when behind
sejuani no damage what now
say: Hold Glacial Prison for whoever jumps on your carry, or throw it to start the fight if one of them steps up alone.
more: Glacial Prison stuns the first champion it hits and slows the rest, and none of that needs gold.
Arctic Assault knocks up, and Permafrost stuns a target with full Frost stacks. That is three pieces of control your team can chain on one target.
Frost Armor gives you resistances when you have been out of combat, so start fights fresh, not after poke.
check: Which of them is a threat to your carry, and whether your team is close enough to follow a stun.
breaks: Wrong if your team has no damage near you: a stun with no follow-up just puts you in the middle of them.
basis: kit:Sejuani

when: you have more deaths than kills
asks: master yi behind what do i do
i'm behind on yi
yi fell behind do i farm
how do i come back as master yi
say: Farm both sides until your next item and enter fights last, or take a kill only on someone already low and alone.
more: Master Yi's damage comes from items and attack speed. Behind, you have neither yet, so early fights go badly.
Meditate restores health and reduces damage, which keeps you clearing without recalling as often.
Alpha Strike makes you untargetable for a moment. Save it to dodge the ability that would kill you, not to open.
check: Which camps are up, and whether the low target has allies close by.
breaks: Wrong if the enemy is ending the game while you farm: then join your team and wait for the cleanup.
basis: kit:Master Yi

when: you are behind and level 6 or higher
asks: nocturne behind what do i do
i'm behind on nocturne where do i ult
how do i use paranoia when behind
nocturne fell behind
say: Use Paranoia to join a fight your laner is already winning, or keep it and farm if every lane is behind.
more: Paranoia lets you launch onto an enemy champion from a distance, so you can keep farming the camps beside a lane and still join its fight.
From behind, you are the second player in. Land on a target your laner already hurt.
Shroud of Darkness passively adds attack speed, which keeps your clears decent while you catch up.
check: The health of both laners in the fight you want to join.
breaks: Wrong if you would land first on a healthy target near their tower: do not press it. Clear instead.
basis: kit:Nocturne

when: you are below level 6 and behind their jungler
asks: evelynn behind before 6
i'm behind on eve what do i do
evelynn got invaded now what
how do i get to 6 on evelynn
say: Full clear away from where he showed until level 6, or take a gank only on a lane pushed right up to your tower.
more: Before level 6 Evelynn has no camouflage, so she is easy to see coming and a poor bet in an early duel a level down.
Demon Shade heals you when you are low and out of combat, so you can keep clearing without recalling.
Level 6 changes everything. Getting there with as few deaths as possible is the whole early plan.
check: Where their jungler last showed and which of your camps are up.
breaks: Wrong if he is living in your jungle: take lane waves your laners leave, because the levels matter more than where they come from.
basis: kit:Evelynn

when: their jungler is dead and you are behind him in level
asks: their jungler died but i'm behind
he's dead can i catch up
enemy jungler is dead what do i take
is now the time to invade
say: Take his camps on the nearest side while his timer runs, or start the objective if it's up and a laner can help.
more: His death timer is the one moment a jungler who is behind can enter the enemy jungle safely.
His camps close the gap twice over: you gain them and he comes back to nothing.
An objective is worth more, but only if someone is with you. Behind, you are slow at it alone.
check: His respawn timer, which camps are up, and whether his laners are moving toward you.
breaks: Wrong if his laners have the waves pushed and are already walking in: take one camp and leave.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: the enemy has taken the first dragon and the grubs
asks: we lost dragon and grubs
they got everything what now
we lost both objectives
we have no objectives what do i do
say: Play for the herald with your top side, it's the next thing in that pit, or match their jungler's side and stop the tower dives.
more: Objectives lost early are a lead for them, but not a decided game. What matters is that the next one is not also free.
The top pit holds herald after the grubs. Taking it helps your team win a tower back.
Grubs help them take towers, so your side lanes need you nearby more than before.
check: Whether herald is up, and which of your towers is lowest.
breaks: Wrong if your top side is the part of the map that is losing: take the next dragon instead, with bot and mid.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

when: their jungler had a kill or assist in the last two fights you were part of
asks: their jungler is always there when i gank
i keep getting counter ganked
he's always on my side
every gank turns into a 2v2 i lose
say: Wait until he shows, then play the opposite side at once, or bring your mid so you're the side with more players.
more: If he is following your path, the answer is information. The moment he appears somewhere, the other half is free.
A jungler seen on the far side cannot stop a gank, a camp steal or an objective on yours.
Bringing a third player changes the count. Counter ganks only work when the numbers are even.
check: Where he just appeared, and whether your mid has the wave pushed enough to move.
breaks: Wrong if he has not shown for a long time: assume he is near you and take camps, not a gank.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

when: one enemy has many more kills than anyone else in the game
asks: one of them is super fed
how do we deal with the fed guy
their carry is too strong
can we shut down the fed one
say: Fight only when the fed one shows far away, or stack crowd control on that player and nobody else.
more: A single fed player wins by being in every fight. The fights without that player are the ones your team can take.
When that player appears in a side lane, the other four are beatable. That is your objective window.
If you must fight all five, every stun goes on the fed one. A shutdown brings a lot of gold back to your team.
check: Where the fed player is right now, and how much crowd control your team has ready.
breaks: Wrong if the fed one is a split pusher who takes towers alone: someone has to answer the lane, or you trade evenly at best.
basis: written

when: your level and CS are below their jungler's
asks: belveth behind what do i do
i'm behind on belveth
belveth got invaded how do i recover
how do i catch up on belveth
say: Full clear for stacks and skip even fights with him, or take a skirmish only when a teammate lands crowd control first.
more: Death in Lavender stacks are permanent, so camps are never wasted on Bel'Veth even when the score looks bad.
Above and Below knocks up and slows, which is your one way to hold someone for a teammate.
Forty stacks give a ninety second True Form and eighty make it permanent, so steady clears are how her strength comes back for later objectives.
check: Which camps are up and where their jungler last showed.
breaks: Wrong if their jungler keeps taking your camps: farming a jungle that is empty does not work. Shadow a lane and take the waves it leaves.
basis: kit:Bel'Veth

when: you are level 3 or lower after 4:00
asks: my clear was really slow
i'm low level and it's 4 minutes
i messed up my first clear
i'm behind on my clear what now
say: Finish the camps you have left before anything else, or take the crab on the side your laner pushes if it's still up.
more: One full clear is about level 4. If you are short of that, the missing camps are the fix, not a gank.
Both crabs first spawn at 2:55, so by now one may already be gone. The one beside a pushed lane is the safe one.
Ganking at level 3 into a jungler who is level 4 is how a slow clear becomes a lost early game.
check: Which camps and which crab are still alive.
breaks: Wrong if a laner right next to you has an enemy nearly dead under your tower: take that, then clear.
basis: rule

when: your level and CS are equal to or above their jungler's
asks: am i ahead
how am i doing
am i winning the jungle
is my farm ok
say: You're on pace or ahead. Keep the clear going and add one play per clear, or bank the lead with a recall.
more: Level and CS against the other jungler are the honest scoreboard. Kills come and go.
On pace means you can afford one gank or invade per clear without falling behind.
The next test is the first objective. Arrive at it with an item and you are properly ahead.
check: What the next objective is and how far away it is.
breaks: Wrong if your lanes are all losing while you farm: your own numbers look fine but the map does not. Spend time on a lane.
basis: pro:Kills are not a lead if the farm went the other way

when: your level is below their jungler's and your CS is lower
asks: am i behind
how bad is it
am i losing jungle
is the game going badly for me
say: You're behind on level and farm. Clear twice without stopping, or cover a lane if your camps are being taken.
more: Being behind is a pace problem, and it is fixable. A level gap closes with full clears and no deaths.
The plan changes from making plays to not giving more away, until the levels are even.
Check again after two clears. If the gap is the same, he is taking your camps and you need wards or lane farm.
check: Which of your camps are up, and whether he has been seen in your jungle.
breaks: Wrong if your team is ahead despite your score: then stay with them and play as support for the fed laner.
basis: pro:A jungler who is behind has few places to go

when: an allied laner died in the last 30 seconds
asks: i was going to gank but he died
my laner just died is the gank off
plan's ruined what now
he died before i got there
say: That gank is off. Catch the wave at his tower if it's safe, or cross to the other side while their jungler's there.
more: A kill on your laner often means their jungler was there. That places him, and it opens the other half of the map.
The wave at the tower is the cheapest thing to save and keeps your laner from falling further back.
Do not gank that lane the moment he returns. He comes back behind, and it is a two on two you lose.
check: Whether their jungler got the kill or assist, and how big the wave at the tower is.
breaks: Wrong if the enemy laner stayed very low after the kill: walk in and take the kill and the wave.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

when: an objective is spawning and one or more allies are dead
asks: we were going to do dragon but someone died
is the objective still on
can we still contest
teammate died before the objective
say: With a player down the fight's off. Trade for the far side, or hold the pit entrance only if their jungler's dead too.
more: Objectives are a numbers question first. Four against five at a pit loses the fight and the objective.
The plan that replaces it is the trade: they commit several players, so something else is open.
If their jungler is also dead, it changes. Without Smite they are slow, and you can stall until your teammate respawns.
check: The respawn timers on both sides, and how many of them are at the pit.
breaks: Wrong if your dead teammate respawns before the objective can die: stall and poke, and the fight is back on.
basis: pro:Count who can actually arrive before contesting

when: an allied laner has died twice or more and is behind their opponent in CS
asks: i was playing for top but he's losing now
the lane i camped is still losing
do i keep helping this lane
my plan was that lane and it's failing
say: The plan's broken there. Move your clears to the lane doing best, or stay only if their tower is nearly down.
more: Help that has not worked twice is not going to work a third time. The enemy now expects you there.
Switching sides is not giving up. It moves your time to where it still turns into something.
Tell the lane you are leaving to play back and farm.
check: Which other lane is even or ahead, and where its wave is.
breaks: Wrong if the lane you are leaving has your team's only late game carry: keep covering it, but defensively.
basis: pro:Stop repeating a gank that keeps failing

when: your team leads in kills but not in towers or dragons
asks: we have more kills are we winning
we're up in kills but nothing else
why aren't we ahead with all these kills
is our lead real
say: The lead isn't real yet. Turn the next kill into a tower or objective straight away, or group and take one now.
more: Kills are gold for individuals. Towers and objectives are what open the map and end games.
A team with kills and no towers is usually chasing. The fix is a habit: kill, then hit something.
If they are behind in gold but level in towers, one lost fight makes it even again.
check: Which tower is lowest and which objective is up.
breaks: Wrong if their team has much better wave clear: sieging stalls. Take objectives and their jungle instead of towers.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: the enemy has three dragons
asks: they have three dragons
they're on soul point what do we do
how do we stop soul
is the next dragon a must
say: The next dragon is the one you have to fight. Be there early with all five, or take Baron if it's up.
more: Four dragons give soul, and soul usually decides the fights that follow. This is where trading stops.
Arriving early with vision matters more than anything else. The team that walks in second walks into a trap.
After 20:00, Baron is the only trade that compares. If they send five to dragon, it can be the answer.
check: The dragon timer, and whether Baron is alive.
breaks: Wrong if you cannot win a five on five at all: send the trade to Baron or their base and accept the soul.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: your team has scaling champions and the game is past 14:00
asks: we scale are we on track
is our late game plan working
we just need to survive right
how long do we have to stall
say: You're on track if they're under three dragons and your towers are mostly up. Keep trading, or fight the dragon that gives soul point.
more: A scaling plan works as long as the other team is not building a clock against you. Dragons are that clock.
Give ground slowly: outer towers for farm is fine, inner towers and soul are not.
The moment your carries finish their core items, the plan flips and you start contesting.
check: Their dragon count, your tower count, and how close your carries are to their items.
breaks: Wrong if your carries are also behind in farm: scaling is not happening by itself. You need a fight or a pick to reset the pace.
basis: pro:Early dragons are the clock against a scaling team

when: kills and towers are close to even
asks: it's even what wins this
what's our win condition
how does this game end
what should we be playing for now
say: Whoever wins the next Baron or Elder fight likely wins. Set up early with waves pushed, or look for a pick first.
more: Late and even, the next big objective decides it. Everything before it is preparation.
Preparation means side waves out, wards down, and nobody caught beforehand.
A pick just before the spawn is the cleanest way to make an even game uneven.
check: Which objective is next and when, and where your side waves are.
breaks: Wrong if your team is clearly weaker in a grouped fight: do not set up five on five. Push sides and make them split.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: their jungler is a level or more above you
asks: is the invade still good
should i still invade
i wanted to counter jungle but he's ahead
do i go into his jungle
say: The invade's off while he's a level up. Clear your own side, or go in only when he shows on the far side.
more: An invade assumes you win or avoid the duel. A level down, you do neither.
Once he shows somewhere else the risk drops to his laners, and that is a risk you can read.
Losing the invade costs your camps as well as your life, so the downside is double.
check: Where he was last seen, and which lanes beside his jungle are pushed.
breaks: Wrong if his laners are both dead or recalled: then even a level down, a quick camp steal is fine.
basis: pro:An invade ends when the nearest lane arrives

when: you died in the last 30 seconds
asks: i just died what do i do when i respawn
i'm dead what's the plan
what now after dying
i got caught, what next
say: Buy, then go to the camps that respawned while you were dead, or straight to the objective if it's up within a minute.
more: A death timer is a free recall. Spend everything, so you come back stronger than you died.
Camps kept respawning while you were down. Starting on the side away from where you died avoids a second death.
If an objective is close, being there on time matters more than one camp.
check: The objective timers and which camps are up.
breaks: Wrong if the enemy is in your base or taking a tower: defend first, camps after.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: you are level 6 and their jungler is level 5 or lower
asks: i just hit 6 what now
i'm level 6 is it time to gank
i have my ult what do i do
level 6 plan
say: Their jungler's still short of six, so this is your window. Gank the nearest pushed-up lane, or start an objective with a laner.
more: Reaching your ultimate first is a short lead. It closes when he gets his, so use it before he catches up.
A gank with an ultimate against a lane without one is the best odds you get in the early game.
If no lane is gankable, an objective with a laner turns the same window into something permanent.
check: Which enemy laners are pushed up, and whether an objective is alive.
breaks: Wrong if he reaches level 6 before you get there: the window is gone. Go back to trading sides with him.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

when: your team was ahead and has lost two or more players in the last minute
asks: we just threw
we lost a fight we should've won
we threw the lead what now
that fight was bad are we still ahead
say: You're likely still ahead on gold. Defend, clear waves and reset, or give the objective so it isn't a second lost fight.
more: One lost fight rarely erases a real lead. The second one, taken in a hurry to make up for it, does.
Let them take what the fight earned them. Then you are five again with the same items as before.
The plan after a throw is the plan from before it: set up early, and let them come to you.
check: Respawn timers and what they are taking right now.
breaks: Wrong if they are heading for your base with Baron: everyone alive defends, and waves come first.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: the enemy has just taken dragon soul
asks: they got soul is it over
they have soul what now
can we still win after soul
what's the plan against soul
say: It isn't over, but stop fighting them head on. Play for picks and Baron, or split the map so they can't group.
more: Soul makes their grouped fights much stronger. It does nothing in a fight that never happens.
After soul, Elder is the next dragon. That one you have to contest or trade Baron for.
Catching one player before those objectives is your most realistic way back.
check: The Elder and Baron timers.
breaks: Wrong if your team has no pick tools and no split pusher: then turtle, clear waves, and wait for them to make the mistake.
basis: rule

when: the grubs have been killed and game time is before 20:00
asks: grubs are gone what's next
what do i play for after grubs
what's the next objective
is herald worth it
say: Next up top is herald, worth it if a tower's low, or play bot side for dragon if your bot lane can move first.
more: Grubs do not respawn. After them the top pit holds herald, then Baron from 20:00.
Herald is worth the most when it finishes a tower. A tower with full health may only lose plates.
Choose the side by which of your lanes can walk to the river first.
check: Tower health in each lane, and which of your lanes has the wave pushed.
breaks: Wrong if their jungler shows on one side: take the objective on the other, whichever one that is.
basis: rule

when: you have a lead and their jungler has not been part of a kill or objective for several minutes
asks: i haven't seen their jungler
where's their jungler i'm ahead
is it safe to keep invading
he's been gone a while
say: Treat him as near you until he shows. Keep to camps beside your pushed lanes, or drop a ward and wait.
more: A jungler who is missing from where he should be is information. When he is behind, he is probably looking for you.
His CS tells part of it. If it is climbing, he is farming. If it is flat, he is waiting somewhere.
Your lead survives a minute of caution. It may not survive being caught alone.
check: Whether his CS has gone up recently, and which of your lanes are pushed.
breaks: Wrong if he just showed in a lane: the map is open again. Go and take what is on the other side.
basis: pro:A jungler missing from where he should be is information

when: before 6:00 and you have bought an item component
asks: i backed early was that right
i recalled after my clear is that ok
did i lose tempo backing
should i have stayed for crab
say: That's fine, you'll fight the river with an item. Walk to the crab or objective now, or gank on the way if a lane's pushed up.
more: A quick clear and recall trades a little camp time for an item at the first river fight, which often decides it.
The cost is that he may have taken a crab or a gank while you were in base. Check the score before you walk in.
From here keep the pattern: clear, spend, arrive.
check: Whether you gave up camps to recall, whether the crabs are still alive, and where their jungler showed while you were in base.
breaks: Wrong if he used that time to take your far camps: clear what is left first.
basis: pro:A fast clear and recall brings an item to the river

when: you are a level above their jungler before 5:00
asks: i'm a level up do i fight for crab
i'm ahead early, crab or gank
should i contest scuttle
can i take both crabs
say: Take the crab on the side your lanes push and fight him for it if he comes, or gank that lane if he doesn't show.
more: Both crabs first spawn at 2:55, and the first pair is the early fight a level lead is built for.
Winning it gives your team river vision on that side for whichever objective comes first there.
Crossing the map for the second crab is greedy unless he has shown somewhere else. You arrive late, and maybe to his laners.
check: Which of your lanes are pushed, and whether that crab is still alive.
breaks: Wrong if the lane beside that crab is stuck under your tower: their laner gets there first. Take the other crab or keep clearing.
basis: rule

when: their jungler is a level above you before 5:30
asks: do i fight for crab when behind
he's at my crab what do i do
should i give scuttle
i lost both crabs
say: Give the crab he's at and take the camps he walked away from, or take the other crab only if your laner there's pushed up.
more: A crab is not worth a death a level down. The camps he left to walk there pay more, with no fight.
Both first crabs spawn at 2:55. Only after both die is there a single crab on a random river side, so not before about 5:25.
By that later crab a clean clear can have you level with him again, and it is a fairer fight.
check: Which crab he is at, and which of your lanes could reach the other one first.
breaks: Wrong if he just showed on the opposite side of the map: the crab near you is free, so take it.
basis: rule

when: your level and CS are above their jungler's and two or more allied laners are behind in CS
asks: i'm ahead but my lanes are losing
i'm fed but my team is behind
i'm winning jungle but lanes are bad
how do i carry losing lanes
say: Spend your lead on the one lane that can still win with you there, or take objectives only while their jungler's dead or far.
more: A jungle lead with losing lanes is a short lead. Their laners can reach most river fights before yours do.
One lane brought back gives you a partner for objectives, which is what turns your lead into something lasting.
Invading deep is the tempting use and the risky one here, because nobody can come if you are caught.
check: Which laner is closest to even, and where that lane's wave is.
breaks: Wrong if every lane is too far gone to fight even with you: farm both jungles where it is safe and become the carry yourself.
basis: pro:The jungle beside a losing lane is theirs

when: you have two or more kills or assists before 10:00
asks: my ganks are working do i keep going
i'm ahead on an early jungler how do i keep it
do i keep ganking or farm now
my champ falls off how do i use this
say: Keep ganking, but turn each kill into plates, dragon or grubs before you leave, or clear first when your camps are up.
more: An early-game jungler's lead is on a timer. Kills alone do not stop the other team catching up, but towers and objectives do.
Clearing between ganks keeps your level ahead too, so the next gank is still stronger than their answer to it.
The lane you got ahead becomes the one you play objectives beside.
check: Which of your camps are up, and what objective or tower is closest to the lane you just ganked.
breaks: Wrong if their laners now sit under tower with wards out: forcing ganks wastes the window. Invade with your fed laner instead.
basis: pro:Kills are not a lead if the farm went the other way

when: your level is below their jungler's
asks: i'm an early game jungler and i'm behind
my early game failed what now
i needed a lead and didn't get one
i'm behind on a ganking champ
say: Stay near your strongest lane and counter-gank there, or take a gank on your path only where the enemy has no Flash.
more: A level down, you cannot force a lead. Answering his play with your laner beside you is a fight on better terms.
Your crowd control or burst still works in a two on two from behind. What fails is going in first, alone.
After lane phase your job becomes starting fights or protecting a carry, so keep your deaths low on the way there.
check: Which enemy laners have used Flash, since the coach sees spell names but not cooldowns, and where their jungler last showed.
breaks: Wrong if their jungler only farms and never ganks: there is nothing to counter. Match his farm and wait for an objective fight.

when: you are a level or more above their jungler
asks: can i just fight their jungler
i'm stronger than him do i duel
should i go look for him
i win the 1v1 right
say: Go where he has to be, his next camp or the crab, and fight him there, or just take the camp if laners are coming.
more: A duelist's lead is spent in one on ones. Each one you win takes a camp, a death timer and often an objective after it.
Fight early in the meeting, before help arrives. The duel is yours, but the two on two depends on whose lane moves first.
If he will not fight, take what he was protecting. It is the same result with less risk.
check: Which lanes near that spot are pushed, and whether he still has Flash or an escape.
breaks: Wrong if his champion out-duels yours at this stage despite the level: use the lead on ganks and objectives instead.
basis: pro:An invade ends when the nearest lane arrives

when: your level and CS are about equal to their jungler's
asks: we're even what decides it
jungle is even now what
i'm even with him what do i play for
how do i get ahead from even
say: It's even, so the first objective decides it. End your clear on the side your lanes push, or gank to make one push.
more: Two even junglers are separated by their lanes. Whoever has laners arriving first takes the crab, the dragon or the grubs.
So the useful play from even is helping a lane win its wave. A gank that forces a recall counts even with no kill.
Avoid a coin-flip fight in the river with nobody near. Even junglers lose those to whoever gets help first.
check: Which of your lanes are pushed, and which objective comes next.
breaks: Wrong if his champion scales better than yours: even is losing slowly. Force a play before the next objective.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: you have two or more deaths and no kills before 10:00
asks: i'm 0 and 2 is it over
i've died twice already
i'm feeding what do i do
how bad is this start
say: It's not over, but the plan changes. Farm your safe side and fight only beside a teammate, or cover waves if he's invading.
more: Two early deaths cost you camps and levels. That gap is real, and it closes with farm, not with a kill attempt.
The next death is the expensive one, because that is when he can walk into your jungle whenever he likes.
Compare levels again after a couple of clears. If you are within one of him, you are back in the game.
check: Which of your camps are up, and where their jungler last showed.
breaks: Wrong if your team is winning its lanes anyway: stay near the strongest one and help it take objectives.
basis: written

when: the enemy team has just killed Baron
asks: they got baron what do we do
how do we defend baron
they have baron buff now what
do we fight them with baron
say: Clear the waves at your towers and don't fight outside them, or catch one who splits off if you have numbers there.
more: Baron makes their minions the threat. Killing the waves is the defense, and fighting in the open is what they want.
The buff runs out. Losing an outer tower while it lasts is acceptable. Losing three players is not.
A team with Baron often spreads across lanes. One of them alone near your tower is the only fight worth taking.
check: Which lanes their players are in, and which of your towers the big waves are heading for.
breaks: Wrong if they dive anyway with a big lead: give that tower and fall back to the next one together.
basis: written

when: your team has just killed Baron
asks: we got baron what now
how do we use baron
baron's ours where do we push
do we group with baron
say: Recall, buy, then push two lanes at once so they can't hold both, or group in one lane if they can catch someone alone.
more: Baron is strongest when it stretches them. Strong waves in two lanes force them to split, and you fight the smaller half.
Recalling first costs some buff time but brings everyone's gold into the push.
As the jungler, stay with the bigger group and keep Smite for the next objective.
check: How many of them are alive, and which of their towers are lowest.
breaks: Wrong if most of them are dead right now: skip the recall and hit their base while the timers run.
